title: World War One
note: Dimensional rigour is the strength; the Argument chapter performs the essay by narrating its own structure, and the per-power chapters repeat one dimension order.

title: Starmer endgame / Arsenal title
note: Strong leads and clear prose, but this is the run that leaked special-edition .sp-* components into a weekly and routed front-matter around the gates.

title: Eating at Efteling & Beekse Bergen
note: Vivid and concrete throughout; occasional adjective-led food writing edges toward performance but never loses the information.

title: The First Roman Emperors
note: A genuinely strong issue with a tight thesis and high fact density; the only real drag is that the four middle reign-chapters (Tiberius/Caligula/Claudius/Nero) march through a similar succession-mechanics-then-what-it-proved mold with a hostile-sources NOTE each, flattening the rhythm the bookend chapters otherwise vary well.

title: The week everyone spent waiting
note: Density and hooks are excellent, but several sections close on the same concrete-claim-then-deflating-pull-quote move, giving the twelve-section read a faintly repetitive rhythm.

title: The Next — After Dragon Ball & Star Wars
note: The named three-criteria thesis is carried and pressure-tested through every pick, but the three tiered recommendation chapters repeat an identical pick-card-plus-on-ramp template that flattens after the second pass.

title: A truce that lasted a day
note: Genuine component variety carries the read, but the compare-panel and also-list patterns recur across Toolkit, Shelf and Places, keeping structure just short of distinct-shape-per-section.

title: Efteling & Beekse Bergen
note: Plain, confident prose; recurring X-not-Y parallel construction opens both halves identically and a few aphorisms lean toward cadence.

title: Burnham walks back into the Commons
note: Density and the realignment angle carry the issue; voice is the softest dimension, recurring to posed binaries and withheld-payoff lines reached for rhythm rather than information.

title: The week the ceasefires turned into paperwork
note: Dense, well-shaped and genuinely missable throughout, but a recurring meta-framing tic ('the considered version of the summer is…', 'the honest framing is a deload', 'the honest read keeps that in view') comments on the content's significance instead of just delivering it.

title: The Byzantine Empire
note: The prose is plain and the survivor-thesis spine is exceptionally well carried, but voice dips where the issue narrates its own argument and reaches for a few hollow connective lines.

title: America at 250, in a year that won't sit still
note: Fact density is exceptional and openings state real stakes, but voice leans on a recurring mannerism — aphoristic withheld-word closers and a repeated X-is-the-story frame, plus an occasional self-narrating aside.

title: H1 2026 in Review
note: Yes on both north-star counts — it names what the half added up to ('the changing of the guard,' honestly complicated rather than asserted) and hands him carriable verdicts via the Memory Test and Picks; novelty is the drag, since the Highs, Lows and Throughline largely re-tell events he followed live, with the genuinely-missed material concentrated in What We Missed.

title: The night the world went live
note: Plain and communicative, with an earned Telstar-to-Joe-Meek payoff; the signal metaphor runs a touch thick and the savings-rate item recurred across four sections — both tightened in a pre-publish repair round. ~6,300 words, four verified images.

title: Seven Leaders, No Election
note: Both north-stars land: the 'week of handovers' synthesis carries from cover through Letter, Long Read and Threads, and the closing pin gives one real named action (lock a mortgage quote if a fix expires within six months); all four movements present, The Desk a single two-column department. Softest spot is throughline — the handover spine doesn't quite reach Bookmark and parts of Screen & Sound, reading as a themed cover more than a building argument.

title: One Hundred & Four
note: A genuinely synthesised throughline — the feared 48-team experiment vindicated, and Spain winning by suppression and squad depth rather than the 2010 romance — lands with a clear takeaway, so both north-star questions are a firm yes; novelty is the mild drag only because a retrospective inevitably re-tells results the reader watched live, though the off-pitch ledger and analytical angles keep it well clear of recap.

title: The first ordinary week under a PM nobody elected
note: A strong, coherent issue that both synthesises the week and lands a concrete savings action, with an excellent Antikythera Long Read; the only real drag is visual density at ~1.5 images/1000 words against the 2/1000 norm, leaving the Screen & Sound and Bookmark movements photo-free.

title: The Friendly Games that nearly died (Glasgow 2026)
note: A confident, tightly-themed week-of-endings issue with genuine synthesis and a real pinned action; softest dimension is visual — opens on type with no cover image, ~11 images across 7,500 words just under the 2/1,000 norm, and Bookmark jackets left as type-only placeholders.

title: The strait and the toll
note: No cover photo-plate and an image-free OPEN leave image density just under the ~2/1,000-word norm; otherwise a tightly built, richly-furnished issue whose captioned figures sit inside the features.

title: A readiness score dressed as a diagnosis
note: A coherent quiet-August issue that names the weeks real thread (the wrist going medical-grade) and lands one clear action (diarise the season openers), carried by a genuinely investigative HRV Long Read; softest dimension is visual.

title: The Impossible Job
note: The fixture-list Long Read is genuine discovery and the section-by-section structural variety is exemplary, but visual richness is the softest link — the issue opens on type with no cover image and its 11 images sit under the ~2-per-1,000-words norm, with Screen & Sound running entirely text-only.

title: The tariff, explained
note: Dense, well-illustrated, spine-driven; only soft spot is prose reaching for a rhetorical close once too often.

north_star.what_did_the_week_add_up_to: YES — the Letter names the spine, the Long Read supplies the machine under the noise, the colophon reprises it.
north_star.one_thing_to_do: YES — one pinned close: pick one main lift and run double progression, echoed on a ticket.

structural_integrity: PASS — all four movements; The Desk one department of two columns.
